_about: E20 full-episode-only fragment (the full_only.json equivalent, named mistake.json per E11, the direct ENG-04 sibling; open question 4 says follow E11 exactly). Consequence-flip episode (ENG-04): in place of an attack half, the learner makes five everyday choices on the road in a safe sandbox (the `mistake` stage), then a montage flip shows where each led. There is NO attacker, no target, no osint/people/intelFacts, so there is no attack.json. These keys are pasted into scenarios/awareness_e20_remote_and_mobile_working/scenario.json.erb (the FULL shell) ONLY; the generated defend-only shell (gen_e8_e17_shells.py) never carries them. Shapes follow test/js/fixtures/social_awareness/clean_mistake.json, scripts/validate_social/awareness.rb mistake_checks/montage_line_checks, and public/break_escape/js/minigames/episode-runner/consequence-sandbox.js. Tarrowby Logistics and everyone/everywhere in it are fictional; see defend.json and BRAND_ADDITIONS.md. NAMING NOTE for the wiring agent: E20 brief section 15 calls this file attack.json; it is authored as mistake.json to match E11 (its ENG-04 sibling) and open question 4's 'follow E11 exactly'. The generator reads only defend.json, so this filename is a human handoff only.

_notes.mistake: Paste at social.awarenessEpisode.mistake (ENG-04). Five everyday choices on the road, unscored. Exactly one safe:true option per beat (the approved route). The safe option's position is VARIED beat to beat (1st, 2nd, 1st, 2nd, 1st), so it is never always first and never always second (AGENT_RULES_CONTENT line 15; E20 task instruction 'vary where the safe option sits'). This REORDERS the options from the E20 brief section 9 draft, where the safe option was second in all five beats; the labels and ids are unchanged, and the montage keys on option id, not position, so the reorder is safe. flipBeat is cafe_wifi, the one beat with a real adversary (a look-alike network and an over-asking page), quoted back as the montage headline (aw2).
_notes.flip: Paste at social.awarenessEpisode.flip (ENG-04). mode 'montage' makes the flip replay the sandbox choices instead of looking for a sent message; required when stages lists 'mistake' (awareness.rb). flipHeading ('Through their eyes.') lives in defend.json strings, shared by both variants (though the defend-only shell has no flip, so it is never shown there).
_notes.flipMontageByChoice: Paste at social.awarenessEpisode.strings.flipMontageByChoice (ENG-04), FULL shell only. Keyed beatId then optionId; a line is authored for BOTH options of every beat (E20 brief section 10), so ENG-04's unsafe-option fallback never fires. For a beat the learner took the safe option on, the montage shows the 'taken instead' line (the version where it went wrong), so a careful learner still sees the cost. No bystander steals or misuses anything (no-blame). Erb-only: it must NOT appear in the defend-only shell (parity test); add flipMontageByChoice to STRINGS_ERB_ONLY_OK in test/js/social-awareness-fragment-erb-parity.test.mjs (ENG-04 owns this).
_notes.defendIntro: Paste at social.awarenessEpisode.strings.defendIntro in the FULL erb only (E20 brief section 8b, 'After the attack half'). The host's hand-off line from the montage into the defend half; the runner shows it entering the defend stage (as E16 does, full_only.json). The defend-only shell takes its own defendIntro from gen EPISODES['e20']['defend']['defendIntro'] (section 8b), so this full-shell line is not in the fragment strings and not in the host ink.

beats.situation: On the 07:42, you open the client list to check it before the meeting. Where do you work on it?

options.label: Move to the seat with its back to the wall, privacy screen on, and leave the sensitive bits for later
Here, in the aisle seat, with people in the row behind

beats.situation: In the café queue, a client rings and asks you to read out the building's alarm code and the room list. What do you say?

options.label: Read it out quietly over the phone
"I'll call you back from somewhere private," or send it through the approved route

beats.situation: You go to the counter. The friendly person at the next table offers to watch your laptop. What do you do?

options.label: Thank them, and take the laptop and tablet with you
Thank them and leave it with them, you'll only be a minute

beats.situation: The café Wi-Fi list shows two networks that look like the venue's. The stronger one's page asks for your work email and password to get online. What do you do?

options.label: Join the stronger one and sign in with your work account
Join the network the staff name, wait for the VPN, or use your phone's hotspot

beats.situation: That evening the survey tablet isn't in your bag. It's locked. What do you do?

options.label: Ring the service desk now, day or night, and say what it was and where you last had it
Wait until the morning, it's locked and might turn up

flipMontageByChoice._use: The full text of the montage lines. Lives at social.awarenessEpisode.strings.flipMontageByChoice in the full erb.

cafe_wifi.sign_in_fake: The stronger network wasn't the café's; it was named to look like it. Your work password went to whoever set it up, and by mid-afternoon someone had signed in as you from across town.
cafe_wifi.venue_or_hotspot: You joined the network the staff named and waited for the VPN. The look-alike with the stronger signal got nothing from you. This is the one the attackers were counting on.

train_screen.aisle_open: The student in the row behind read three clients' names off your screen before you closed it. She wasn't being nosy; the screen was just there.
train_screen.back_to_wall: With your back to the wall and the privacy screen on, the names stayed yours. The student behind you saw a spreadsheet of nothing in particular.

cafe_call.read_it_out: Everyone in the queue heard the alarm code and which rooms to go to. By the next day the client had changed the code, and every cleaner needed the new one.
cafe_call.call_back: "I'll call you back" was a complete answer. You rang from outside, and nobody in the queue heard a thing.

mind_laptop.leave_it: The stranger was lovely and touched nothing. The couple at the next table, though, could read your open inbox for the whole four minutes you were at the counter.
mind_laptop.take_it: The laptop and tablet came with you to the counter, so there was nothing on the table for anyone to read, and nothing to walk off.

lost_tablet.wait_morning: The tablet sat in the café overnight, still signed in to the survey app. By the time you reported it next morning, it had been out of your hands for twelve hours.
lost_tablet.ring_now: You rang the service desk that evening. They locked the tablet within minutes, and when the café found it the next day it was switched back on. The hours that matter never happened.

defendIntro: See how little it took? A screen someone read on the train, a code someone heard in the queue, a bag left for a minute, and one password typed into a network that wasn't the café's. None of it was clever. Now it's the kiosk: tell the safe networks and pages from the look-alikes.
